children.title: USDA and HHS Announce Line-by-Line Review of Dietary Guidelines Report
children.description_short: USDA and HHS announced a line-by-line review of the 2025 Dietary Guidelines Advisory Committee report and set a target to publish final guidelines before the statutory deadline.
children.description_medium: USDA and HHS announced a line-by-line review of the 2025 Dietary Guidelines Advisory Committee’s scientific report on March 11, 2025. The report was advisory, not the final guidelines; officials said they aimed to publish by the statutory deadline. Contemporaneous reporting described the committee’s evidence review and said it made no recommendation on ultra-processed foods.
children.description_long: On March 11, 2025, USDA and HHS announced a line-by-line review of the 2025 Dietary Guidelines Advisory Committee’s scientific report. The committee’s report was an advisory document submitted to the departments; it was not the final federal Dietary Guidelines. USDA and HHS said they aimed to release the 2025–2030 guidelines before the statutory December 31 deadline and described future process improvements on transparency and conflicts of interest. Agri-Pulse reported that the committee spent 22 months reviewing nutrition evidence and that its recommendations included dietary-pattern advice. It also reported that the committee made no recommendation on ultra-processed foods, citing a lack of research. The sourced event is the agencies’ announcement of a review and timetable. The release’s political-science rhetoric does not establish that scientific conclusions were changed for political reasons. This card covers only the review announcement. The frozen parent also mixed in separate budget, CDC, grant, citation, local-food funding, and NIH personnel claims; those are not established by these sources and are not included here.

children.title: NIH Nutrition Researcher Kevin Hall Announces Early Retirement and Alleges Censorship
children.description_short: NIH researcher Kevin Hall announced early retirement and alleged HHS aides censored his work; HHS denied the accusation.
children.description_medium: NIH nutrition researcher Kevin Hall announced an early retirement on April 16, 2025, after 21 years. CBS News reported Hall’s allegations that HHS officials restricted interviews and other research communications. HHS denied censorship and disputed his account. The reports document competing statements, not a finding that officials censored Hall or caused his departure.
children.description_long: On April 16, 2025, NIH nutrition researcher Kevin Hall announced early retirement after 21 years at the agency. CBS News reported that Hall said he was stepping down and accused senior aides to HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. of censorship. Hall told CBS that officials blocked a direct interview with a New York Times reporter about his ultra-processed-food research; he also said he was barred from presenting at a conference and faced demanded edits to a manuscript. These are Hall’s reported allegations. HHS denied editing his answers and rejected the censorship charge, saying NIH scientists could discuss research through written responses or other means and that it remained committed to gold-standard research. The Washington Post likewise described Hall’s concerns about political interference at NIH. The available sources establish the retirement announcement and competing accounts, not a factual finding that censorship occurred or that any specific official caused Hall to leave. The dietary-guidelines review is a separate event and is not part of this record.
